nodes.label: Auditor costs increase
nodes.title: New audit requirements **increase State Auditor costs**

quotes.locator: Fiscal Effects, Increased State Auditor Costs, sentence 1
quotes.text: Proposition 41 would increase State Auditor costs by creating new and ongoing audit requirements.

nodes.label: General Fund pays for unsuccessful initiatives
nodes.title: The **General Fund pays audit costs** for rejected or unqualified initiatives

quotes.locator: Fiscal Effects, Increased State Auditor Costs, sentence 5
quotes.text: One-time audit costs associated with special taxes that do not ultimately appear on the ballot or are rejected by voters would be paid from the state’s General Fund.

nodes.label: Voter guide costs increase
nodes.title: Audit summaries **increase printing and mailing costs**

quotes.locator: Fiscal Effects, Higher Costs to Print and Mail VIG, sentence 2
quotes.text: These audit summaries could add several pages to the VIG, which would increase state printing and mailing costs by a few hundred thousand dollars per qualified initiative.

nodes.label: Savings depend on follow-through
nodes.title: Savings require **effective recommendations that policymakers implement**

quotes.text: Proposition 41 could result in savings or improved services if policymakers implement the State Auditor’s recommendations and those recommendations prove effective.

nodes.label: Net fiscal effect unknown
nodes.title: The **net fiscal effect is unknown** because future decisions matter

quotes.locator: Fiscal Effects, Net Effect Not Known
quotes.text: The net fiscal effect of Proposition 41 is unknown as it depends on future decisions by voters, the Legislature, and other policymakers.

nodes.label: Courts could stop Prop 40
nodes.title: Prop 41 could **stop Prop 40 becoming law** if it receives more affirmative votes

quotes.text: If Proposition 41 receives more “yes” votes than Proposition 40 on this same ballot, then Proposition 40 could be stopped from becoming law even if it gets yes votes from a majority of voters. This is because the courts could find that Proposition 41 conflicts with Proposition 40.

nodes.label: Audits could improve outcomes
nodes.title: Independent public audits could produce **better program outcomes**

quotes.locator: Argument in favor, opening paragraph, sentence 1
quotes.text: Prop. 41 requires the State Auditor to conduct independent public audits of programs funded by proposed new taxes in order to increase transparency and accountability and drive better outcomes.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Denise LeDuc Froemming, CPA, President California Society of Certified Public Accountants (CalCPAs); Tom Hayes, Fmr. California State Auditor; Robert Gutierrez, President California Taxpayers Association (CalTax)

nodes.label: Homelessness spending lacks results
nodes.title: Homelessness programs have received funding with **too little to show**

quotes.text: Billions of our tax dollars have flowed into state programs like homelessness efforts, with too little to show for it.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Denise LeDuc Froemming, CPA, President California Society of Certified Public Accountants (CalCPAs); Tom Hayes, Fmr. California State Auditor; Robert Gutierrez, President California Taxpayers Association (CalTax)

nodes.label: Independent information for voters
nodes.title: Voters need **independent program information** before approving new taxes

quotes.locator: Argument in favor, Independent Public Information, sentence 1
quotes.text: Before we vote on new taxes to fund programs, voters should have access to independent information about how those programs are being managed and whether they actually need more funding.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Denise LeDuc Froemming, CPA, President California Society of Certified Public Accountants (CalCPAs); Tom Hayes, Fmr. California State Auditor; Robert Gutierrez, President California Taxpayers Association (CalTax)

nodes.label: Spending limit protects taxpayers
nodes.title: Tax compliance with the spending limit preserves **excess-revenue refunds**

quotes.locator: Argument in favor, A Better Deal for Taxpayers, second bullet
quotes.text: Requires all taxes to comply with the state’s voter-approved spending limit—including its requirement that excess revenues get refunded to taxpayers.

attribution.name: Ballot argument for
attribution.signers: Denise LeDuc Froemming, CPA, President California Society of Certified Public Accountants (CalCPAs); Tom Hayes, Fmr. California State Auditor; Robert Gutierrez, President California Taxpayers Association (CalTax)

nodes.label: Designed to undo Prop 40
nodes.title: Prop 41 was designed to **undo the Billionaire Tax**

quotes.text: This is a billionaire-funded initiative designed specifically to undo the California Billionaire Tax, Prop. 40.

attribution.name: Ballot argument against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Healthcare at risk
nodes.title: Defeating the billionaire tax risks **working people's healthcare**

quotes.locator: Argument against, Would Cancel Out the Billionaire Tax
quotes.text: It’s about defeating one specific tax that billionaires want to avoid, because they’d rather millions of working people lose healthcare than pay a modest, one-time tax on their extreme wealth.

attribution.name: Ballot argument against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Sergey Brin funding claim
nodes.title: Sergey Brin is **one of Prop 41's main funders**

quotes.locator: Argument against, Funded by Billionaires, sentence 1
quotes.text: One of Prop. 41’s main funders is Google founder and Trump donor Sergey Brin, whose wealth has DOUBLED to nearly $300 billion since Trump’s election.

attribution.name: Ballot argument against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Added time and expense
nodes.title: Prop 41 would cost the state **time and money**

quotes.locator: Rebuttal to argument in favor, Would Cancel Out the Billionaire Tax, final sentence
quotes.text: To add insult to injury, Prop. 41 isn’t just a scheme, it’s an expensive one—it would cost the state time and money.

attribution.name: Rebuttal against
attribution.signers: Suzanne Jimenez, Chief of Staff SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West

nodes.label: Billionaire-funded cancellation claim
nodes.title: Billionaire funding aims to **cancel Prop 40**

quotes.locator: Rebuttal to argument in favor, Would Cancel Out the Billionaire Tax, sentence 1
quotes.text: Prop. 41 is a billionaire-funded scheme designed specifically to undo the California Billionaire Tax, Prop. 40.

attribution.name: Rebuttal against

nodes.label: Trackable progress could help services

quotes.text: Prop. 41 requires transparency and trackable progress of programs, to help improve education, health care and other public services Californians rely on.

attribution.name: Rebuttal for

nodes.label: Waste displaces useful spending

quotes.text: Every dollar wasted is one that could go to help someone.

attribution.name: Rebuttal for

nodes.label: Public reviews expose mismanagement
nodes.title: Public audits expose **waste or mismanagement** and recommend improvements
